degraded: projector/dependency failure means surface may be incomplete or partially wrong
unavailable: projection cannot support that surface; UI must fall back or disable

precise navigation/deep-linking usually allowed if target object identity valid
live mutation/approval/recovery/retry/cleanup require current or direct canonical-runtime validation

stale visibility is not same as action authority

seed_items.canon_label_hint: Lane and worktree lifecycle states with cleanup eligibility rules
exact_items: treat lane lifecycle and worktree lifecycle as related but non-identical
lane = orchestration lineage object, worktree = concrete Git/filesystem backing object
lane states: baseline, active, suspect, restoring, retained, cleanup_eligible, archived, removed, historical
baseline: canonical starting lane for package pool
active: currently eligible/in use for live work
suspect: not safe for normal dispatch until examined or restored
restoring: in explicit recovery/restore/reconcile flow
retained: intentionally kept after completion/failure for inspection/compare/delayed cleanup
cleanup_eligible: no longer needed for live execution and may be archived/removed under policy
archived: historical object retained in model, but not active live lane
removed: live backing removed; only historical identity and lineage remain
historical: user-facing historical posture rather than dispatchable live posture
worktree row posture: live, dirty, conflict, orphaned, recovering, retained, archived, removed
recover/archive/prune/remove must not blur together
recover: attempt to restore or reconcile suspect/orphaned/conflicted worktree into safe known state
archive: retire from active use while preserving identity/metadata/lineage for historical browsing
prune: cleanup-oriented action for policy-eligible items; narrower than generic remove; typically stale/orphaned/live-no-longer-needed worktrees
remove: explicit destructive removal of live worktree backing after confirmation and eligibility checks
cleanup must be gated by more than age

checks before archive/prune/remove: no active-run ownership, no unresolved blocked recovery requiring worktree, no required safe-point restore targeting it, no unresolved conflict workflow user needs, no newer lineage operation depending on live lane/worktree
live cleanup must never erase run/lane/worktree lineage from History/Ledger/graph-linked inspection
Source Control owns concrete worktree actions; Orchestrator owns lane-pool truth and cleanup posture
Source Control should default to compact current/live worktree rows with filters for retained/cleanup-eligible/archived/removed
active-run ownership must be visible before destructive worktree actions
safe-point and blocked recovery lineage can keep old worktree relevant even after supersession
cleanup should reduce live clutter without erasing historical object model
notes: Existing docs imply cleanup cannot be trivial delete
Without split model, UI risks either deleting useful historical truth or keeping too much live clutter forever

removed: live backing removed; only historical identity and lineage remain
